name: Paul Smith
life: “I still remember a child's first important use of the word yours.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Paul by a small Friday habit. Paul stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I saw the switch but the toddler holding both had just learned mine and yours.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a boxy denim jacket and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Paul has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with auburn hair cut square at the nape. Paul grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Paul is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Paul is concerned.
agenda: To let the child explain the swap.
family: Ana West is Paul’s half-sibling. Paul keeps the photographs. Ana knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Ana says, “I walked over with a cup of water. I am grateful the letter didn't mention me because I cried afterward.”
connections: June Kent. A child's confusion about ownership leads the secondhand buyer to the aunt who made the first dress.

reactions.response: Paul gets the two families together in the shade to identify the items.
